items.t: Boots to an interactive screen with visible loading feedback
items.d: No long black screens. Show progress during long loads and meet the platform's boot-time expectations.

items.t: Survives a multi-hour soak test without crashing or hanging
items.d: Leave the game running in its heaviest scenes and menus for hours, on every hardware model you support.

items.t: Tested on every hardware model you list
items.d: Base and upgraded consoles, digital editions, and handheld and docked modes. A crash on one model is a failure.

items.t: No memory leaks or performance collapse over long sessions
items.d: Track memory and frame time across a full playthrough, not just short test runs.

items.t: Quitting from the system menu never corrupts data
items.d: Force-close the game at every point you can, including during saves and loads.

items.t: Handles missing save data on first boot and after deletion
items.d: A new player and a player who deleted their save both get a clean start.

items.t: Detects corrupted saves and recovers or explains
items.d: Never crash or hang on a damaged file. Offer a recovery path or a clear message.

items.t: Handles insufficient storage with a clear message
items.d: Check what happens when the system is full before a save, an install or a patch.

items.t: Tells the player when not to power off during saves
items.d: Use a saving indicator wherever writing data takes noticeable time.

items.t: Saves belong to the correct user profile
items.d: Two profiles on one console must never share or overwrite each other's progress.

items.t: Handles sign-out or user switching mid-session
items.d: Return to a safe state such as the title screen and ask the right user to continue.

items.t: Uses the active user's data, settings and achievements throughout
items.d: Profile changes must propagate everywhere, including online and menus.

items.t: Respects parental controls and account restrictions
items.d: Child accounts and restricted features behave as the system settings require.

items.t: Controller disconnect pauses play and prompts reconnection
items.d: Gameplay must never continue unattended after a controller drops.

items.t: Reconnecting restores the right controller to the right player
items.d: Test re-pairing in single player, local multiplayer and menus.

items.t: Button prompts and icons match the platform
items.d: No wrong-platform glyphs anywhere, including tutorials, loading tips and key art in menus.

items.t: Suspend and resume (rest mode) without data loss or desync
items.d: Suspend during gameplay, loading, saving and online sessions, then resume hours later.

items.t: System overlays and notifications never break the game
items.d: Open the system menu, receive invites and notifications, and check audio and input recover cleanly.

items.t: Follows system language and accessibility settings where required
items.d: Default to the system language when supported and honour relevant system settings.

items.t: Handheld, docked and low-battery transitions work
items.d: Switch modes mid-game and check resolution, UI scale and performance.

items.t: Connection loss mid-session fails cleanly
items.d: Pull the network during matchmaking, gameplay and purchases. Show a clear message and never hang.

items.t: Server outages and maintenance are handled gracefully
items.d: Players get an explanation and a way back, not an endless spinner.

items.t: Online features check the user's platform privileges
items.d: Online play, subscriptions where required, and communication settings gate the right features.

items.t: Invites and joining from the system UI work
items.d: Join from a friend's invite with the game closed, at the title screen and mid-match.

items.t: Voice and text chat respect platform privacy settings
items.d: Muting, blocking and communication restrictions apply everywhere chat exists.

items.t: Every achievement is obtainable and unlocks at the right moment
items.d: No unobtainable or mis-triggered unlocks. Verify each one in a clean playthrough.

items.t: Unlocks earned offline sync correctly
items.d: Earn achievements offline, reconnect, and confirm they register.

items.t: Names, descriptions and icons are final and localized
items.d: Treat achievement text as store-facing copy, because it is.

items.t: All purchases use the platform's store flow
items.d: No external payment paths inside the game.

items.t: Purchased content appears, restores after reinstall, and handles removal
items.d: Test purchase, reinstall, a second console, and refunded or revoked entitlements.

items.t: In-game prices and items match the store
items.d: Mismatched names, prices or bundle contents are a common, avoidable failure.

items.t: Platform terminology is used exactly as required
items.d: Button names, system feature names and brand names follow each platform's guidelines.

items.t: Every declared language is complete
items.d: No missing strings, truncated text or overlapping UI in any language you list on the store.

items.t: No placeholder, debug or developer text anywhere
items.d: Search the build for test strings, debug menus and internal names before you submit.

items.t: Required legal text and credits are present
items.d: EULA, privacy notice, third-party license notices and credits where the platform or your licenses require them.

items.t: Age ratings secured for every region you ship in
items.d: IARC for digital releases on participating storefronts, plus ESRB, PEGI, USK, CERO or others as required. The rating must match the content.

items.t: Interactive elements are disclosed
items.d: Online interactions, in-game purchases and user content are declared in your rating questionnaire.

items.t: User content can be reported and moderated
items.d: Players can report and hide content, and you have a process to act on reports.

items.t: Store assets meet each platform's specs
items.d: Icons, key art, screenshots and trailers at the required sizes and content rules.

items.t: Metadata and feature declarations are accurate
items.d: Descriptions, supported features, player counts and languages match the build.

items.t: Submission form, version numbers, price and release date are set
items.d: Wrong version numbers and missing paperwork delay submissions that would otherwise pass.

items.t: Day-one patch is scheduled through certification too
items.d: A patch is a submission. Plan its certification alongside the main build.

items.t: Manufacturing lead time is in the schedule
items.d: Physical releases need the final build earlier than digital. Confirm lead times with your publisher or the platform holder.

items.t: Packaging and printed materials are approved
items.d: Box art, ratings marks and platform branding go through approval as well.
